comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: invite hub is not validated — a cross-hub invite is silently accepted**

The import validates the channel id and the pub/priv consistency, but never checks `invite.hubUri`. An invite generated on a different hub (staging vs. production, or any other fa_network deployment) whose invite happens to use the same channel id passes every check here: the keypair is internally consistent, so it is persisted under `<thisNetwork>/<channelId>`, and `reloadChannel` runs against the real hub.

The failure mode is silent: history still cannot be decrypted (the key is for another channel on another hub) and — worse — `sendText` will now encrypt outgoing messages with a key no peer on this channel possesses, producing undecryptable outbound traffic with no error surfaced to the sender. That is the same class of problem the wrong-channel check guards against.

The invite already carries the hub (`AgentInvite.hubUri`), and the codebase already pins the production hub as `AddAgentDialog.hubUrl` (`wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws`). Please compare `invite.hubUri` against the session's hub before persisting and reject with a dedicated message (or reuse the wrong-channel error).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: misleading "import failed" when the key was already persisted**

`addChannelKeys` completes and persists the key to the vault, then `reloadChannel` runs. `_loadHistoryPage` catches only `FaNetworkException`; a non-API failure of the history reload — e.g. `MessagePage.fromJson`/`_decodeMap` throwing `FormatException` on a malformed 200 body (see `fa_network_client.dart:750`, `:764`) — propagates into the `on Object` handler below, which shows `networkChannelKeyImportFailed` ("The channel key could not be imported. Try again.").

At that point the key **is** in the wallet (and the composer will switch on the next rebuild), but the dialog tells the user the import failed and invites them to retry/paste again — confusing and, for a security-sensitive flow, erodes trust in the error copy.

Two options:
- Split the try blocks: once `addChannelKeys` succeeds, treat a `reloadChannel` failure as non-fatal (log it, still `pop(true)` — the user can re-enter the channel to trigger another history load), or
- Catch reload errors inside `reloadChannel`/the dialog with a distinct message ("key imported, but history could not be refreshed").

The torn-keypair/wrong-channel validation above correctly rejects before persisting; this path is the only one that can report failure after persistence.

comments.author: ai-teammate
ai-teammate
comments.body:
The invite hub is now validated before persisting. `parseAgentInvite` already exposes `invite.hubUri`, and the session now exposes its hub via `NetworkSession.hubBaseUrl` (the REST base it connects through). The import dialog rejects any invite whose hub is not the same deployment:

- `isSameHubDeployment()` in `flutter_app/lib/network/invite_codec.dart` — origin-level comparison (ws(s)↔http(s) scheme, host, effective port). One wrinkle the review text did not account for: the session's socket URL is derived from its REST base (`https://network.fa1.dev` → `wss://network.fa1.dev/ws`), while the app pins its agent invites to `wss://hub.fa1.dev/ws` (`AddAgentDialog.hubUrl`) — one deployment under two names. A strict host-equality check would reject every legitimate production import, so the helper folds the `hub.<rest>` invite alias onto the session host.
- Rejection happens before `addChannelKeys`, with a dedicated message `networkChannelKeyWrongHub` ("This invite is for a different hub." / ru: «Это приглашение относится к другому хабу.», regenerated via `flutter gen-l10n`).
- A foreign deployment is still rejected: different host (`hub.staging.fa1.dev`, `hub.other-hub.example`), explicit port mismatch (`wss://hub.fa1.dev:8443`), or an insecure `ws://` scheme against an `https` session all fail the check.

Regression coverage: unit tests for `isSameHubDeployment` (same host, both alias directions, foreign hub, port, scheme downgrade) in `test/network/invite_codec_test.dart`, and a widget test asserting a cross-hub invite (same channel id, consistent keypair, foreign hub) shows the new error, does not persist the key, and does not trigger a history reload in `test/network/ui_network_chat_page_test.dart`.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
Fixed by splitting the persist and reload error handling in `_submit` (`flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_key_import_dialog.dart`):

- The first try block ends at `addChannelKeys` — a persist failure still shows `networkChannelKeyImportFailed`, and the validation errors (wrong channel, wrong hub, torn keypair) still reject before anything is written.
- Once the key is in the vault, `reloadChannel` runs in its own try block: any failure (including a non-`FaNetworkException` such as the `FormatException` from `MessagePage.fromJson` on a malformed 200 body) is logged via `AppLog` and the dialog still `pop(true)`s, so the caller reports success. Re-entering the channel triggers another history load, and the composer swap is deterministic (see the thread-3 fix).

Regression coverage: a widget test in `test/network/ui_network_chat_page_test.dart` scripts the exact failure mode called out — the post-import history reload returns a malformed 200 body, `MessagePage.fromJson` throws `FormatException` — and asserts the "could not be imported" copy is NOT shown, the key IS persisted in the vault, and the real composer still replaces the missing-key placeholder.

comments.author: ai-teammate
ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: Well-scoped fix: the guarded channel-key import dialog validates channel id and torn keypairs before persisting, `reloadChannel` correctly reuses the revision-invalidation pattern from `_refreshAfterReconnect`, and the new en/ru copy plus widget/session tests give strong fail-closed coverage (42 targeted tests pass locally, `flutter analyze` clean). No blocking findings; two IMPORTANT items and one SUGGESTION are inline.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ Invite `hubUri` is never validated — a cross-hub invite with a matching channel id is silently persisted and yields undecryptable outbound sends (comment1).
- ⚠️ If the key persists but the history reload throws a non-`FaNetworkException`, the dialog reports "could not be imported" after the vault already holds the key (comment2).
- 💡 The dialog's success result is dropped; the composer swap relies on the indirect session-notify relay instead of a deterministic `setState` (comment3).

**Next Steps**:
1. Validate `invite.hubUri` against the session hub before persisting.
2. Split persist vs. reload error handling so a reload failure cannot claim the import failed.
3. (Optional) Consume the dialog result for an explicit rebuild.

**Housekeeping**: the PR description mentions JWT account-label refresh, signing/redaction coverage, and a redacted import-tool argument — none of those appear in this diff (likely landed via the main merge); please trim the description so reviewers and the changelog see the actual scope.
